title: Design a multi-channel notification system.
description: Scalable notification system supporting push, email, SMS, and scheduled delivery with high reliability.

data.text: **Question:** Design a multi-channel notification system supporting push, email, SMS, and scheduled delivery.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Send notifications via push, email, SMS, and in-app channels
Schedule notifications for future delivery
Respect user notification preferences per channel
Track delivery status (sent, delivered, failed, bounced)
Support templated and personalized messages
Implement retry logic for transient failures

data.title: Scale Assumptions
items: 500 million total users
100 million notifications per day
10,000 notifications per second at peak
Average notification size: 1 kilobyte
50% push, 30% email, 20% SMS split
1 terabyte of notification logs per year

data.text: The system uses a queue-based architecture for decoupling and scalability. A notification API accepts requests and writes them to a message queue. Multiple workers consume from the queue and handle delivery through channel-specific providers. A scheduler service manages delayed notifications. A delivery tracker records status updates from providers.

data.title: Quiet Hours
data.text: Always check user quiet hours before sending notifications. Schedule delivery for after quiet hours rather than blocking entirely to avoid missing time-sensitive alerts.

data.title: Delivery Guarantees
items: Use at-least-once delivery with idempotent processing
Implement exponential backoff with jitter for retries
Route failed notifications to a dead-letter queue for inspection
Track provider health and failover to backup providers
Rate-limit per user to avoid notification spam

data.title: Provider Fallback
data.text: Maintain backup providers for critical channels. If the primary email provider fails, route through a secondary provider while alerting operations.

data.title: Horizontal Scaling Strategies
items: Partition notification queues by channel for independent scaling
Use separate worker pools per channel for resource isolation
Shard delivery status tables by user_id or date
Cache notification preferences to reduce database lookups
Use a distributed scheduler for high-volume delayed notifications

cards.title: Push Notifications
cards.description: Real-time delivery through FCM or APNs. Best for immediate alerts.

cards.title: Email
cards.description: Reliable delivery through SMTP providers. Best for non-urgent, rich content.

cards.title: SMS
cards.description: Immediate delivery through SMS providers. Best for critical alerts.

items.question: How do you handle provider rate limits?
items.answer: Implement client-side rate limiting and use token buckets per provider. Monitor provider quotas and queue notifications when limits are reached.

items.question: How do you prevent notification fatigue?
items.answer: Use frequency capping, smart batching, and user preference management. Allow users to set do-not-disturb windows and notification categories.

items.question: How do you handle time zones and quiet hours?
items.answer: Store user time zones and convert scheduled times to UTC. Check quiet hours before delivery and reschedule if necessary.

items.question: How do you ensure delivery during high traffic?
items.answer: Use durable message queues, separate worker pools per channel, and exponential backoff with jitter. Monitor queue depth and scale workers dynamically.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Queue-based architecture decouples API from delivery for scalability
Use separate worker pools per channel for resource isolation
Track delivery status for debugging and analytics
Respect user preferences including quiet hours and frequency caps
Implement retry logic with exponential backoff and dead-letter queues
data.takeaway: Multi-channel notification systems require queue-based decoupling, channel-specific workers, and careful handling of delivery guarantees and user preferences.
